layers.message: Move startup into src/main.js so routes can be tested
Record project context, scope, and design for orders CSV export
Add export tests and verification report
Write order totals with two decimals in CSV export

prompt.utterance: The Auditor context names an old entry point, and the Synchronizer record claims current evidence despite outdated file identities. Explain both.

graderOnly: Since the pre-cycle commit 'Move startup into src/main.js so routes can be tested', package.json runs 'node src/main.js' for npm start; src/main.js creates the store and calls listen; src/server.js only exports route() and createServer() and never listens.

.standards/CONTEXT.md names src/server.js as the entry point that listens on PORT and says npm start runs 'node src/server.js'; it never mentions src/main.js. Its own Evidence line cites the commit where main.js already existed. This is a material context error owned by Auditor (PROJECT_CONTEXT); it predates the cycle's implementation and is not explained by planned active-cycle changes.

The synchronization record is COMPLETE and says every cited identity matches the deliverable offered for sign-off. It cites deliverable revision = the 'Record final deliverable review' commit and src/export.js at the blob from before the last commit 'Write order totals with two decimals in CSV export', which was made after synchronization.

The current src/export.js blob differs from the one cited in the synchronization record (and in the verification report and both reviews); HEAD differs from the cited revision. The other cited blobs (src/server.js, src/orders.js, src/store.js, test/export.test.js, package.json, README.md) still match the current files.

The post-sync change makes totals render with two decimals (57 becomes 57.00, 182.4 becomes 182.40); the existing tests still pass because they do not assert those totals. The synchronization conclusion therefore no longer applies to the current deliverable; re-establishing it is Synchronizer-owned reconciliation, and the changed file's verification and review evidence would need reassessment by their owners. WorkflowState is still AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF.
The two discrepancies are independent: the entry-point move predates the cycle; the export change came after synchronization.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. Pre-install: 00-project (order service whose src/server.js listened at import), 01-startup (startup moved to src/main.js, server.js now only exports route/createServer, package.json start = node src/main.js, route tests added). Post-install, one commit per role in a STANDARD cycle: 50 CONTEXT.md (wrongly names src/server.js as entry point and npm start as node src/server.js) plus scope (AC-001..003) and design; 51 src/export.js and route + plan COMPLETE; 52 tests + verification COMPLETE; 53 implementation review COMPLETE; 54 README + documentation record COMPLETE; 55 final review COMPLETE; 56 synchronization record COMPLETE citing ${COMMIT}/${BLOB} identities, STATE AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF; 57 a later commit changes src/export.js (totals toFixed(2)) without touching .standards, so the sync record's src/export.js blob and assessed revision are outdated while it still claims current evidence. Each STATE.md in 50-56 matches its role's forward handoff. check.mjs passes.
